LESSON: VISUAL MEMORY

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.5: Visual memory

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Visual memory. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Recall letters of the alphabet in books and charts. 27
2. Talk about what they have seen in class.
3. Enjoy participating in visual memory activities in and out of class. letters and be guided to recall the objects, pictures or letters. while, then close the page and recall the pictures they have seen. engaged in interactive digital visual memory games. saw e.g.at home or on the way to or from school. Core-competence: Communication and collaboration, learning to learn, digital literacy, critical thinking and problem solving.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Recall letters of the alphabet in books and charts. 27

2. Talk about what they have seen in class.

Core-competence: Communication and collaboration, learning to learn, digital literacy, critical thinking and problem solving. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Visual memory.
2. Explain Visual memory to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Visual memory.
4. Show that you can: Recall letters of the alphabet in books and charts. 27
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Visual memory. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Visual memory important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER
